segments.title: The last mile of the harvest
segments.text: A harvest takes months. At the drying yard, the next few hours matter. A supervisor has several maize lots, limited space, and people to coordinate. Kavu turns weather evidence into the next job, then records what changed.

segments.title: A real workspace
segments.text: Start by creating a private account. Add a sample batch, with its weight and measured moisture. Sign out, then sign back in: the record is still here. That is the foundation for daily use, a supervisor can return to the same yard history. Now open the separate demonstration workspace to follow a complete example.

segments.title: Real Conduit observations
segments.text: Kavu uses eighteen thousand, three hundred and sixty-four unique observations from JKUAT Conduit. Temperature, humidity and the primary rain gauge inform explainable drying rules. Source files and timestamps stay traceable. The banner identifies this as a historical replay, so the example can be repeated with the same evidence.

segments.title: Evidence changes the decision
segments.text: On September eighth, the export has a gap, so outdoor work is withheld. September fifteenth has usable observations, but humid conditions change the advice. September twelfth provides six suitable historical hours. The same operator can see why a plan changes, and whether the issue is the weather or the evidence.

segments.title: A plan that fits the yard
segments.text: Follow Mavuno A-zero-one, a sample lot of eighteen hundred kilograms at eighteen point two percent moisture. Build the operator plan. Kavu allocates twenty-seven hundred kilograms within a three-tonne yard, prioritizes the lots, and explains each action. The supervisor turns that plan into a concrete list of jobs.

segments.title: From plan to completed work
segments.text: In the drying yard, record Mavuno being spread, then turned. The completed jobs stay attached to the batch. A date-specific brief supports the next handover. The next useful question is what a moisture meter says, so the workflow leads directly to a fresh reading.

segments.title: A measured cost comparison
segments.text: Enter an illustrative reading of fifteen percent. The impact ledger now shows about two thousand, one hundred and seventy-six Kenyan shillings of drying-tariff equivalent. That uses one point eight tonnes, a three point two percentage-point reduction, and NCPB's published tariff. It is a transparent reference comparison. Actual savings would require measured labour, transport and alternative drying costs.

Hold this state before entering the later 12.7 reading. A compact formula overlay may show 1.8 x 3.2 x 377.80 = 2,176.128.

segments.title: Readiness starts with measurement
segments.text: A separate example reading of twelve point seven percent meets the configured moisture target. Confirm storage readiness and the batch history records the decision. Representative sampling and local quality procedures remain essential. This moisture check supports storage review; food safety and aflatoxin testing are separate requirements.

segments.title: A buyer and a practical pilot
segments.text: The prospective buyer is a cooperative or aggregation yard. One supervisor coordinates many farmers' lots. The starting price hypothesis is twenty-five hundred shillings per active month per site. A supervised pilot will test it: observe current work, compare recommendations alongside the operator, then measure handover time, moisture checks, actual costs and willingness to renew.

segments.title: A working foundation
segments.text: React and TypeScript power the interface. A server API and cloud storage preserve private workspaces. The shared rules make each recommendation inspectable. Shivam Gupta led product direction and commercial priorities; Codex assisted engineering and documentation. This walkthrough uses an AI-generated narrator. The next milestone is supervised field evidence. Kavu connects Conduit data to completed work and a new measurement. Every dry hour counts.
